notes: All 16 physical body-text lines were read against the full-resolution halves, along with the three rows of display (65): physical_lines_read=19. The top page number 26, bottom foliation 53, four inserted spans, cancellations, and drawings were read separately and are inventoried rather than counted as additional physical lines.

The manuscript treats the case h_1=1 under the stated bound 0≤ν≤2. It claims that a graph has at most one end, discusses the one-end graph as a circle with an attached segment, and discusses the end-free graph as a circle with one or two marked vertices. These are accounts of manuscript claims, not an independent proof of its classification.

The first dimension formula is read dim mod G=ν, while the three case labels below read dim amb G. The difference is supported by the final d versus final b letter shapes and has not been normalized away.

The third row reads ν=2−dim amb G. This may be an author slip, since the preceding rows have chained equalities, but the single dark bar is preserved. No claim that the minus equation is mathematically correct is made.

The three combinatorial drawings have respectively (V,E)=(1,1),(2,2),(2,2), where the third has a self-loop plus a tail edge. Reading their displayed connectivity gives E−V+1=1 in each case. This small count checks consistency of the drawings with h_1=1 only; it does not prove the classification or the stated dimensions.

The third curve drawing was cropped and traced visually once at place11. The lower straight branch carries a above b and continues upward only into the loop; the two curved branches cross farther above and continue separately. C’s TikZ connectivity and label order reproduce this, so no substantive drawing change is proposed.

H’s editorial page label and drawing descriptions are treated as editorial surrogates, not source words. The descriptions were compared for objects and labels; their literal prose is not added to the transcription. Pure macro/wrapper differences, including the label add on baseline combinatoire, are not counted as text errors.

All C deletions and insertions were checked for extent: Et is crossed before Mais; the line through il n’y a pas stops before baseline de; G n’a pas is above that line; isom is attached before au; the q-descender cancellation lies between graphe and combinatoire; de at the end of line 13 is crossed; donc is inserted before the count. The four insertion leaders are not mistaken for word punctuation.

12 original-image crops were generated once each using Pillow autocontrast, LANCZOS scaling to 2200 or 2600 pixels wide, and modest sharpening; every crop was viewed. One view_image transport failure occurred before place08 returned an image; the already-saved crop was then viewed successfully without recropping.

First reading contained 19 substantive comparison rows and two substantive departures from C; additional C changes mark uncertainty only. Those counts describe the frozen first reading; subsequent audit changes are recorded separately.

The blind comparison changed the parenthetical être to explicitly doubtful en avoir: a separate longer second group and its i dot were missed in the first reading. The final log supersedes the earlier one-word explanation. It also added à/colon uncertainty after the first homéom. and reproduced three places with junction trace details or pen-lift gaps. These drawing details do not assert a different graph topology or alter the earlier limited E−V+1 calculation. No new mathematical check was performed.

notes: The manuscript says the action on the one-dimensional local moduli factor is trivial when gα0=1 and factors through the symmetric group on Îα0, isomorphic to S4, when gα0=0. It tentatively claims that any subgroup of S4 can occur, with the author’s qualification sauf erreur. No independent verification of that realization claim was performed.

It treats ambient modular dimension 1 as the isolated-vertex case, then ambient modular dimension 2 and modular codimension 1 as the one-edge case. The three illustrated possibilities are a two-vertex genus-zero tree with marked weights 3 and 2 (type (0,5)); a genus-zero one-loop graph with marked weight 2 (type (1,2)); and a two-vertex tree with a genus-one distinguished vertex and a genus-zero vertex of marked weight 2 (type (1,2)). These are descriptions of the manuscript’s cases, not a separately established exhaustive classification.

The three right-hand curves were read stroke by stroke: first, two crossing open branches with two marks a,b on one and three c,d,e on the other; second, a curve with one lower loop and a crossing at its neck, marked a,b below; third, two branches with a filled crossing, a genus-one label on the left and a,b on the right. No crossing dot was added to the first or second curve. In the small introductory segment the left endpoint is an open ring and the right one is filled; that distinction is preserved.

Both live displays carry (72); the author’s repeated numbering is retained. The cancelled leading label also appears more like (72) than (71), but remains uncertain. The completed blind audit finds no independent mathematical sign after d’ordre: the terminal chevron belongs to the cancellation stroke, and the deleted text ends with d’ordre. The first-stage < / 2 / ≤ candidates are superseded and survive only in the frozen first-stage records.

The interlinear clause i.e. où la codim modulaire … de G est 0, sits between the sentence’s main baselines, with s1 inserted again above it. On trouve les trois cas de dim modulaire replaces the cancelled two-line start Dans le cas …; the cancelled 1 belongs to sauf 1, not to the replacement. The live continuation is ambiante 2, dim modulaire 1.

The bottom note says that an unlabelled genus or marked weight is zero and that marked weights are written above the graph vertices. Both ou poids marqué insertions attach after genre, as their curved connectors show. The zero is live; the connector above and beside it is not a cancellation. The first diagram’s 3 is physically below-left rather than directly above its point; that visible placement is retained despite the note’s general description.

notes: The manuscript lists five displayed modular-multiplicity cases of dimension 2 in (74), with the written Gamma actions through permutation groups in the first four rows and a trivial action in the last. The products and superscript exclamation marks are transcribed as written. This summary reports manuscript claims; the group-action assertions were not independently proved.

The NB states that the third case maps into S_8 through the written Z/2 dot (S_4 times S_4), labelled prod. 1/2 direct. The label is physically below the formula without a brace. The likely mathematical interpretation is a semidirect product with two four-element blocks; that interpretation helps locate the indices but is not substituted for the literal dot or the worded label.

The manuscript compares the dimension-2 list with two dimension-1 elementary cases (75), calls M-hat!_{0,5} and M-hat!_{1,2} the new cases, and suggests that understanding the discrete Pi_1 groups of four elementary cases might give the key to the general case. This is the author's stated expectation, not a proof established in this reading.

The cancelled row-3 object is proposed as a doubtful product with a lower alpha-in index because of surviving ink, but neither its complete index nor its mathematical appropriateness is certified. The live disjoint-union subscript has an opening parenthesis without a visible closing one; the imbalance is retained rather than repaired. Literal expression en tous is also retained.

Physical-line count 33: five rows in (74); two NB prose baselines plus its one interlinear replacement; the unnumbered formula and its separate lower label; two prose baselines above (75) plus two interlinear additions; two rows in (75); one line beginning les cas nouveaux; eight main baselines of the final paragraph plus its inserted qualifier; three baselines in the rotated upper-left note including inserted hat-M_G; two in the slanted note beside (75); and two separate numbers, author's ink 29 and lighter pencil 59. Array indices and accents are read as part of their rows, not counted as extra text lines.

Every C insertion/deletion was checked on the native halves and its crop: initial marginal deletion and hat-M_G insertion; all three cancelled formula groups in (74); cancelled item after NB; opère replaced by s'envoie; hat-M_G above modulaires; the canceled qui sont/savoir trial and its replacement, whose short groups remain ils/qui and deux/donc; and discrets (i.e. dans le contexte analytique). The line across the t in élémentaires is part of the letter, not an extra deletion.

18 original places were cropped exactly once, with autocontrast, LANCZOS enlargement to 2600 pixels wide and modest sharpening; all 18 were viewed. The upper-left note was rotated -90 degrees and the slanted note -35 degrees. No OCR, internet research or TeX compilation was used.

Only M1033 from the supplied MARKS table appears in decisions. Other unresolved cancelled material is recorded in doubts. The H notes identifying the author's page and commenting on repetitions/cancellations are editorial and have not been transcribed as ink.

The exact first readings in second_boxes contain TeX for whole formulas, including the cancelled row-3 product and all proposed index ink. The large (74) formula box includes the physically adjacent page number 29. The main reader reviewed and approved the first-pass page; the blind independent reading has now been adjudicated. The completed blind audit narrows the large cancelled product to its visible alpha-zero/comma fragment; the full first-stage index in the frozen first TSV is retained as historical evidence, not current text. notes: The manuscript announces a description of specialization relations between strata for the four elementary MD-graph cases and begins section 8 for modular dimension at most 2. It starts with the marked four-pointed genus-zero case and its unmarked counterpart. Both moduli symbols in the opening paragraph have separate angular hats, and the second also has an exclamation exponent; the crop confirms both witnesses here.

The sole alleged cancellation in C, des after structure, is not a cancellation in the ink. The curved line belongs to the insertion de spécialisation entre and ends in the gap after structure, above the live word des. Thus no cancelled text remains in the proposed page. The two interlinear insertions are de spécialisation entre and se partageant, and both attachments were traced explicitly.

The table (76) shows an isolated point labelled I(4) in Codim 0 and a two-point edge labelled I′(2), I″(2) in Codim 1. A single right-pointing arrow labelled 3 crosses the vertical table divider. The initial C of each Codim is large and capital, and is preserved. The table’s left brace is real ink and is retained.

The manuscript interprets the 3 as the three partitions of a four-element marking set into two unordered blocks of cardinality 2, and says these produce three specializations of the maximal stratum. It relates them to three points at infinity of U0,3. The readings quelc., chacun, maxima, sûr aux and on aura are preserved as written; no grammatical or terminological normalization is made.

In (77) the manuscript identifies M̂!0,4 with the projective line over Z and the open M!0,4 with the projective line minus {0,1,∞}. The displayed P and Z are visibly double-struck. These geometric identifications are reported as manuscript claims; they were not independently proved in this reading.

notes: The manuscript continues a discussion of the modular curve over the marked moduli space, with four named sections and an S4 action exchanging them. It says the construction will not be carried out here and would produce the unmarked modular multiplicities. These are manuscript claims; this page reading does not establish them mathematically.

It states that the unmarked space has a single point at infinity corresponding to the three points at infinity of the marked space, permuted transitively by S4. No independent proof of the quotient or its cusp count was performed.

Under the heading on fractional Euler–Poincaré characteristics, the manuscript writes the first two characteristic values −1 and 2, then a quotient-style characteristic and a decomposition using the exceptional sets {−bar j,−j} and {1/2,2,−1}. It ends with −1+1/3+1/2=−1/(24|6), with the denominator overwritten and unresolved. The separate NB writes division of chi_!(U an) by [S4], with result −1/24. Thus a final denominator 24 would make the displayed numerical equality false as written. The transcription preserves the written terms and the denominator doubt. This calculation neither supplies an omitted factor nor settles the overworked digits; no claim is made that all summands should be divided by 24.

It calls the first curve elliptique harmonique and writes the group Z/4Z. The second curve has the retained doubtful words bonne and avec un bon before gr. d'automs Z/6Z. The manuscript claims the two sections meet only at the points 2 and 3 and associates them, with its explicit qualification (sauf erreur), to automorphism groups of orders 24 and 12. notes: The manuscript opens with a weighted expression for bare M_{1,1}: one half of[U], one quarter of[S0-prime], one sixth of[S1-prime], one twenty-fourth of[a2], and one twelfth of[a3]. It then writes[U]=[double-stroked E^1]−[S0]−[S1]+[a2]+[a3]=T(1)−2+zeta2+zeta3. These geometric class identities are manuscript claims, carried as background without an independent geometric verification. The opening M has no class brackets; no correction is supplied.

The manuscript defines zeta_p=[Spec Z/pZ]=i_p!(1), with all four Z glyphs double-stroked. Its displayed K-group connection is probably a rightward arrow, but the focused blind-audit crop shows a dark rounded endpoint without separately readable arms; the arrow is now marked uncertain. The precise geometric formalism and Z_p notation are not independently reconstructed.

The two displayed stratum identities state[S0-prime]=[S0]−[a2]−[a3]=1−zeta2−zeta3 and the same expression for[S1-prime]. These identities are retained as background manuscript assertions; their geometric hypotheses were not checked.

An exact rational-coefficient calculation was performed with Python fractions.Fraction. It verifies1/4+1/6=5/12. Taking the unresolved sign before zeta3 as plus gives coefficients1/2 for T(1),−7/12 for the constant,1/8 for zeta2, and1/6 for zeta3, matching the later displayed expression. Taking that sign as minus instead gives zeta3 coefficient−5/6, with the other coefficients unchanged. The rewrite−1/2−1/12=−7/12 and the addition−7/12+1/2=−1/12 also check. These are conditional algebra checks only: they neither resolve M1043 nor read the canceled and overwritten digits.

System(80) states[M_{1,1}]=one half(T(1)−1)−1/12+1/8 zeta2+1/6 zeta3 and[widehat M_{1,1}]=[M_{1,1}]+1/2=one half T(1)−1/12+1/8 zeta2+1/6 zeta3. The coefficient addition is included in the exact check of note4. The geometric assertion that adjoining the boundary contributes1/2 is carried as background, not independently proved here.

notes: The page begins in continuation with passage aux complémentaires) and relates the ten triangles of I to the ten faces of the icosaèdre gauche, also described in the manuscript as pairs of opposite faces of the ordinary icosahedron. M1051 remains an uncertain correspondant/correspondent; the adjective gauche is legible in all three occurrences on this page. The geometric identification is a manuscript claim, not a result proved in this reading.

The manuscript describes the fifteen partitions of type (2,2,1) of I as square structures on four of its five points, with the two pairs taken from diagonally opposite vertices. It says these correspond to the fifteen edges of the same skew icosahedron. The upper drawing has four filled vertices, two smaller marks on opposite sides, and a detached right-hand point. These are source statements and depicted features; no geometric reconstruction of the polyhedron was attempted.

The slanted NB note assigns to a side a the colors of the four other sides of the adjacent faces, grouped into two pairs. Two distinct canceled low words, both tentatively deux, are present where C recorded only one. The far-right en and the final des deux faces retain attachment/reading uncertainty. The diamond below has separate f and a labels and an upper gap in its vertical stroke; the gap is represented without a topological inference.

The revised incidence passage links an edge a and a face f through the triangle and square assigned to them. The inserted reformulation says that the complement of the triangle is one of the two pairs defining the square. The manuscript then compares the incidence relation of its literal diviseurs à sommets of the structure hat M_{0,I} with faces and edges of the skew icosahedron, or dually vertices and edges of the dodecahedron. The old deux may be canceled or may remain under an insertion connector, and the written numeral 2 remains afterward; neither the wording nor the moduli interpretation has been silently corrected or proved.

Finite computation performed after the visual reading: on an explicitly constructed five-element set, enumeration gives 10 three-element subsets and 15 unordered partitions with two pairs and one singleton. Under the written criterion that the triangle complement equal one of the pairs, each partition is incident with 2 triangles, each triangle with 3 partitions, and there are 30 incidences. The same counts follow from binomial(5,3)=10 and 5*3=15. This verifies the finite counts and that combinatorial incidence criterion only; it does not prove the claimed polyhedral or moduli identifications, and it was not used to choose doubtful letters.

The straight underline immediately below incident is separate from its lower curved connector and has been restored. The first diagram's lower small point is placed on its edge, and the second diagram's divider stops short of the upper vertex. In the NB note no separate final period is visible after faces. The mark after correspond remains à|:. Eight definite canceled spans plus the possible cancellation of main-text deux are inventoried; the two alternative TeX branches describe one physical l'un des insertion, not two. Nine physical main-text insertions are represented, with the separately doubtful en placement in the margin.

The manuscript says that the irreducible components have genus zero, inserts their number 10, says no marked points need to be put on them, and describes a maximal MD graph with all genera zero, all vertices of order 3, and no marked pieds. These statements were carried as background; no geometric or enumerative check was made. The corrected live index I is determined by its bars and upright, not by this mathematics.

It asks for an interpretation from the geometry of the icosaèdre gauche or dodécaèdre gauche, linked to the combinatorial bi-icosaèdre gauche. No equivariance proof or independent group-order calculation was performed.

The marginal NB claims that the hatted M_{0,I} is an actual smooth projective scheme because the represented groupoid is rigid, then extends a statement to all M_{0,I} isomorphic to M^!_{0,nu}, for nu in N. The short phrases after lisse and Il en remain doubtful. notes: The page is an ink manuscript continuation, without a separate ink page number at its head. Pale pencil 70 is kept as margin foliation with uncertain hand attribution. The slanted epsilon_1 note, the parenthesized annotation near (85), all four cancellations and all four inserted items are transcribed. The curve beside raised I is its connector, not an extra opening parenthesis. The smaller annotation near (85) is linked to the bottom-left brace by a curve; its text remains a margin note rather than H’s underbrace.

The manuscript associates a four-element set I amalg tilde A prime_0, furnished with a partition of type (2,2), with its set J of three partitions of that type. A marked epsilon_1 is distinguished; the other two points form J prime=I wedge_(Z/2) tilde A prime_0. A limited independent arithmetic check enumerated the unordered pair partitions of {1,2,3,4}: precisely 12|34, 13|24 and 14|23. That checks only the elementary count three; it neither proves the graph/torsor identifications nor determines a doubtful handwritten digit.

The manuscript describes the projective line indexed by J as a compactification of G_m^1 wedge_(±1) J prime with an S_(J prime), isomorphic to Z/2, action by transfer of structure. It gives the two identifications in (85) and states that S_I acts through S_(J prime), hence trivially on M-hat_(D_0). These geometric/action assertions are carried as manuscript claims, not proved in this reading.

The manuscript names the J prime trajectory P_0 and the epsilon_1 trajectory P_1 as two points at infinity. Formula (86) writes M_(D_0) isomorphic to E_Z^1 minus section 2 and equal to Spec Z[T]_(T−2), preserving that localization notation. It displays M_(G_0)→M_(D_0), T→T+1/T. Formula (87) describes M-hat_(D_0) using P_Z^1 with “signature” 2 along T=2. No proof of these moduli identifications or interpretation of the localization convention is claimed.

For f(x)=x+1/x, direct exact arithmetic gives f(1)=2 and f(−1)=−2. Its derivative 1−1/x² vanishes at x=±1; the second derivative 2/x³ takes nonzero values 2 and −2 there. Thus both ±2 are branch values of this rational map over characteristic zero. The sole section specified in (87), T=2, does not record the other branch value. This calculation neither proves a stack description nor addresses characteristic 2. It flags a question for mathematical review and does not authorize changing the written T=2 to −2.

Local source forms are preserved: associe has no detached final accent; the compactifying glyph has lower m; all three raised A strokes are primes, while Gamma in (85) has an upright and distinct dot for !; (86) has a doubled E rather than A. All five ordinary live D indices use the local small oval 0, without a pointed-loop graphic. The first On a ends in one detached point, transcribed as a period. Both arrows in the via display are plain arrows. The section T in (87) is overworked, but its large top bar survives and there is no minus before 2.

Thirty physical rows were read: twenty-four main-body rows, including one row for the first display, two for (85), one for (86), two for the via map and two for (87); two slanted marginal rows; one parenthesized annotation row; one extra band for the raised I/J/3 insertions; one extra row for inserted P_0; and one pencil-foliation row. notes: The manuscript continues an argument using connectedness of the factors hat M^!_{g_alpha,hat nu_alpha}. It claims the boundary of hat M_G is connected whenever at least two factors have dimension at least 1, using nonemptiness of the relevant factor boundaries. The first boundary symbol's accent is overworked and is retained as a canceled-hat/live-tilde alternative. Connectedness and nonemptiness of the particular moduli factors were not established in this reading.

Conditional topological check performed here: let X be an ordinary topological product of finitely many nonempty connected spaces X_i, with U the product of U_i, and suppose two distinct complements D_i=X_i minus U_i and D_j=X_j minus U_j are nonempty. Choose a_i in D_i and a_j in D_j. The coordinate slices x_i=a_i and x_j=a_j are connected and meet, hence form a connected core in X minus U. Every boundary point lies in a connected slice x_k=d for some d in D_k; that slice meets the first core slice when k differs from i, or the second when k=i. Thus the union of all boundary slices is connected. This proves the elementary product-boundary implication under those hypotheses, without proving that the manuscript's moduli spaces satisfy them or are identified with the required product.

The manuscript reduces to a single M factor and inserts an additional isomorphism to a possibly hatted M_{g,I}. It says the dimension-2 case was already treated and then writes DPS N>=3. The upper expression visibly has a closing parenthesis after 1 but no separable opening one; the literal 3g-1)+nu=2 is preferred with the conventional parenthesized version only an uncertain alternative. The lower N coefficient and opening parenthesis remain doubtful. No dimension formula or prior-case coverage was proved here.

The manuscript says it suffices to join any two infinity divisors by a chain in which successive divisors meet, since those divisors are connected. The sufficiency of that topological criterion was checked conditionally: the union along any such finite chain is connected by induction, and the chain-connected family of connected divisors has a connected total union. This does not prove the needed chains exist or that the individual divisors in this moduli problem are connected.

The manuscript presents the two graph forms (90): a loop on one vertex of weight g-1, for g>=1; and an edge between two vertices with labels I',g' and I'',g''. The right-hand conditions retain the literal equality g'+g''=0. The two displayed stability inequalities are canceled and replaced by the condition about card I' and card I'' when the respective genus is zero. The geometric classification and the stability conditions were carried as source claims without proof.

Graph arithmetic was checked only at the level of the usual weighted-graph genus sum of vertex weights plus first Betti number. The connected loop graph has one edge and one vertex, so its cycle rank is 1 and its total weighted genus is (g-1)+1=g. The connected two-vertex, one-edge graph has cycle rank 0, so its weighted genus is g'+g''. If it represents a generic genus-g case, this suggests the expected relation g'+g''=g. notes: The page, numbered 36 in ink, gives a specialization of case a) as (91): two labeled vertices, a loop at the left vertex and a lower joining edge, with a visibly canceled upper arc. The written constraints are I1 amalg I2=I and g1+g2=g−1. The rational right-vertex condition is revised to on a card I2≥2 when g2=0. A live NB OPS margin proposes g2=1 and g1=g−2 provided g≥2, with an arbitrary partition (I1,I2) of I. These are manuscript statements; the existence and stability of the specialization are not proved here.

A limited exact algebra check verifies (g−2)+1=g−1 and, on adding one cycle, (g−2)+1+1=g. It also verifies (g-prime−1)+g-double-prime+1=g-prime+g-double-prime. These are only polynomial identities. Treating each live loop drawing as one loop plus one joining edge is the usual intended graph reading; the preserved pen gaps are not used to claim topological disconnection. The calculation does not establish a geometric specialization.

The manuscript gives case b-prime in (92), labeled by I-prime/I-double-prime and genera g-prime−1/g-double-prime. For g≥1 it says one may choose the notation so g-prime≠0, after exchanging the two genera, and obtain the common specialization b-prime=a-prime. It states that this proves the asserted result when g≠0. This global assertion and the needed hypotheses on the preceding cases are carried as manuscript claims; no other page was consulted and no proof of them is claimed.

For g=0, with inserted card I≥6, the manuscript says only the cases b) remain. A canceled attempt compares card I-prime with card I-double-prime and concludes card I-prime≥3, then it turns to the chain (93). The middle sketch is only partially canceled: the oblique path crosses b-double-prime, the wavy path crosses the two upper I labels, and the overworked lower glyph has its own cancellation. The lower two-point edge itself is not crossed and remains drawn. H’s editorial claim that the sketch is not struck does not override these separate visible states.

The final captions claim k segments, k+1 vertices and total marked weight 2+k on the left, with analogous ell counts on the right. Conditionally, a chain of n segments has n+1 vertices, and one weight 2 together with n weights 1 sums to 2+n. Exact coefficient arithmetic verifies that elementary identity. It supports the expected plus in a weight sum, but the written right-hand sign is predominantly horizontal and stays minus/plus doubtful. The missing upper weight at a_(k−1) is not supplied, so the arithmetic is not presented as a complete verification of every drawn weight.

The chain has ten explicit visible vertex marks. The one above written b_(-1) is open, the others are filled; no special geometric meaning is inferred from that visual difference. Local small gaps are reproduced. The right caption’s final I-double-prime area remains doubtful because it is overwritten.

Punctuation is local: no semicolon after the marginal g≥2 condition, no terminal period after de I, and no trailing comma after inserted card I≥6 are supplied.
